subject: Scope & next steps: Hyperscaler delta + OpenAI-compat POC
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Bethany Kline <bethany@finlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Scope & next steps: Hyperscaler delta, OpenAI-compat POC

Bethany —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared scope for the POC.

Recap (what we heard):
- Finlytics needs predictable latency at scale for real-time underwriting (99th pctl < 200ms for 1k concurrent requests).
- You are evaluating both the HyperscaleAI managed endpoints and an OpenAI-compatible path (your dev teams prefer minimal SDK changes).
- Procurement questions: data residency (EU option), audit evidence (SOC2) and billing/committed capacity.

Proposed POC scope (what we'll run):
1) API-compat smoke: confirmation of OpenAI-compatible endpoints (chat/completions, embeddings) on our hosted API and our dedicated stacks. Test for request/response shape, streaming semantics, stop-token behavior.
2) Latency/throughput delta vs HyperscaleAI: synthetic load at 1k concurrent steady state + tail-latency profiles. We'll measure tokens/sec and p99 latency.
3) Prompt-diff regression: run your 250-sample prompt set, compare outputs across models/configs and flag quality regressions.
4) SDK swap verification: minimal changes to your client (Python/Node) and example code snippets to ensure integration work is <1 day.

What we need from you this week:
- Test account: an API key or a short-lived test token for Finlytics staging (scoped to evaluation) — can be a temporary HyperscaleAI key and your sample prompt bundle.
- Priority prompt set: the 250 examples you mentioned (or link to Drive). If you prefer, drop them to infra@finlytics.com and CC me.
- Preferred test window and any firewall IP whitelisting we should expect.

Deliverables and timeline (tentative):
- Week 1: API-compat checks + SDK swap guide
- Week 2: Load tests + latency/throughput report
- Week 3: Prompt regression report + recommended config/quantization profile

Attachments: recording-20270429-call.mp3 (call recording), redwood-compat-checklist.xlsx (POC checklist)

If that looks good I'll schedule the first round of API-compat checks for Monday and loop in Ben and Aditya for the testing plan.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: Scope & next steps: Hyperscaler delta, OpenAI-compat POC

Ben / Aditya — forwarding Finlytics' confirmation and prompt bundle. Action items below (short and concrete).

Context: Finlytics will provide a staging HyperscaleAPI key and the 250 prompt set on Monday. They care primarily about: p99 < 200ms at 1k concurrent, minimal SDK changes, and clear quality deltas vs HyperscaleAI.

Tasks: 
- Ben: run the latency/throughput comparison across three configs: Redwood hosted (our managed API), Redwood Dedicated (n1-standard, 8xA100 equivalent), and HyperscaleAI managed endpoint. Deliverable: p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and a short artifact with raw logs + command line for reproducibility. Target: initial run by Tue EOD (May 3). Use the attached benchmark-config.json (small psuedo-config attached here) and aim for steady-state 1k concurrent.
- Aditya: run API-compat smoke and SDK swap verification. Focus on streaming semantics, stop-token behavior, and the Python/Node SDK call surface. Produce a one-page SDK swap guide with code snippets and highlight any behavioral diffs for prompts in the bundle. Target: Wed EOD (May 4). Also kick off the prompt-diff job using the eval harness and produce a CSV of divergence flags.

Risks to watch: difference in streaming chunk boundaries vs HyperscaleAI (we saw truncation on one prior eval), and any tokenization differences impacting outputs. If you hit unexpected divergence that affects acceptance criteria, escalate (cc me + I’ll loop in Research).

Related links: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1abcDEF (prompt bundle), https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/7890

Thanks — let me know if the timelines are tight.

Tessa

Tessa — copied. Plan and quick notes: 

I’ll spin up the Dedicated cluster in our staging region (us-west-2) and run the three-way comparison as requested. Configuration notes:
- Model: rmid-large-v1 (closest to Hyperscale baseline)
- Sequence length: 512 (matches Finlytics prompts)
- Load generator: vegeta/vegeta-go harness with 1k parallel connections for 10m windows to capture steady-state + tail.

Deliverables:
- Raw logs + reproducible run commands in results/finlytics-20270503/
- Summary table (p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, error rate) and a short writeup with hypothesis about any deltas.
- If p99 > 200ms on any config, I’ll take latency profiles and we’ll test batching/cache knob changes.

I’ll also attach the benchmark-config.json I plan to use — if Aditya needs changes for API-compat it’s easy to adjust.

Ben
